content:
incident-bot: Incident declared: high OOM rate observed in serve-prod-us-east-1 runtime pool. Alerts: 12 nodes flapping, 47 container restarts in last 30m. Severity: P1.

alex: seeing CUDA OOM spikes + container CSI errors. First noticed ~ +20m. Rolling error rates up to 6% for text-generation.

maria: confirming memory creeping on paged-attention allocator. Background: we rolled allocator changes two weeks ago. Pattern looks like slow fragmentation, per-worker RSS creeping ~15-40MB/hour until OOM.

raj: customers impacted? any paid producers hitting 5xx?

alex: yes — a handful of mid-market customers show increased 500s and timeouts. Support queue spiking. Not global for all models but affects long-context workloads.

elaine: infra: node flaps match times when kernel OOM killer logs appear. Getting CUDA driver errors in nodes that also show high host mem usage.

sam: sample stack from one crashed container: 
```
E tensorflow: cudnn: CUDNN_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
./serve: runtime_error: failed to allocate 268435456 bytes
```

alex: mitigation idea 1: disable KV cache on affected model families to reduce persistent KV map growth. We can toggle via admin endpoint: `POST /admin/models/<model>/config` with `{\"kv_cache_enabled\":false}`.

maria: +1. Also we should set paged-attention allocator to conservative mode (env VAR: PAGED_ATTENTION_MODE=conservative) which reduces fragmentation by using larger contiguous allocations. But that increases latency slightly.

raj: set priority: stop customer impact now, then assess root cause. Operational plan: 1) disable KV cache on serve-prod-us-east-1 2) set allocator conservative 3) rolling restart of affected replicas 4) monitor memory slope.

alex: executing step 1 now. Running curl admin: `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://admin.prod/models/llama-70b/config -d '{\"kv_cache_enabled\":false}'`

deploy-bot: Deploy request queued: config change for llm-family 'llama-70b' to disable KV cache. Canary: 5 replicas in us-east-1a.

maria: watch output of `ps aux --sort=-rss | head` on one worker; also `smem -rt` for detailed. I suspect small allocations piling up in paged allocator meta structures.

elaine: I've cordoned two worst nodes and started drains to stop incoming work. Draining now: nodes node-us-east-1a-12, node-us-east-1b-05.

alex: can everyone watch for GPU utilization and host mem? Queries: `kubectl top nodes` and `nvidia-smi` on drained hosts.

sam: FYI customers with long prompt sequences (>= 8k tokens) were the first to fail — KV cache is heavily used there.

alex: can we bind a quick traffic-split to fallback small model variant until we stabilize? e.g., route long-ctx to llama-13b as fallback for critical customers.

maria: done: routing rule added for tenant partner-alpha and vip-1 to 13b fallback. This will reduce throughput but keep them online.

raj: logging summary for support: minimal data loss, responses may be degraded quality for fallback users. Please escalate any legal/regulatory customers.

elaine: after disabling KV cache on canary replicas memory slope dropped from 28MB/hr -> ~3MB/hr on those. Good sign.

alex: starting rolling restart on runtime deployment 'serve-llama-70b-prod' canary group -> remaining groups. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/serve-llama-70b-prod -n runtime`

deploy-bot: Rollout started: 30 replicas, strategy: rolling 5 at a time. Progress page: https://deploys.prod/rollouts/serve-llama-70b/1740539876

maria: collecting heap profiles and glibc malloc stats via `jeprof` and `pagemap` on a crashed container for postmortem. Ask SRE for core dump retention.

raj: copying core dumps to retention bucket s3://redwood-oom-dumps/prod/1740539876. ETA 8m.

alex: immediate customer comms: sent first message via support template — informing about degraded latency and fallbacks, no data loss.

support-log: ticket #23489 opened for partner-alpha, assigned to sam.

sam: I'll triage client-specific logs and provide ETA.

maria: observation: allocator fragmentation seems tied to a code path that pins multiple small KV shards and never releases internal pages under heavy long-seq reuse pattern. Hypothesis: a race in free path where freed pages are added to a global list but counts never reduce due to missing atomic decrement in paged allocator.

alex: actionable hotpatch planned: push a short-term allocator guard that forces periodic coalescing every N frees. Patch branch: `hotfix/paged-allocator-coalesce-2024-11`. I can run it as a canary build.

elaine: infra note: if hotpatch contains kernel-level hooks we can't apply easily. Keep it user-space.

maria: built canary image and deployed to 5 canary pods. Monitoring memory slope on canaries.

deploy-bot: Canary build deployed: image: ghcr.io/redwood/serve:hotfix-paged-202411, pods: 5.

alex: early canary metrics: canaries show near-zero slope, no OOMs for 40 minutes. Non-canary nodes still trending.

raj: good. Action items for shift handoff: 1) monitor rollout and canary for 2h, 2) rollback to previous image if errors increase, 3) keep KV cache disabled until next deploy, 4) collect flamegraphs and allocator histograms and attach to postmortem.

oncall-next: I'm taking next shift in 45m. Will keep tabs and coordinate with infra if nodes still flap.

alex: handoff notes to @oncall-next: check `kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=serve-llama-70b -o wide` and memory trends in Datadog (dash: Runtime Memory — Paged Allocator). If slope > 10MB/hr for >30m, escalate to maria and ela ine.

maria: next steps for root cause: reproduce locally with stress harness, add stricter unit tests around free path, audit atomic ops in allocator code.

sam: customer follow-up: will send targeted note to affected customers with rollback ETA and mention fallback usage.

alex: closing incident channel in ~2h if metrics stable. Current status: mitigations applied (KV cache disabled, conservative allocator mode, canary hotfix deployed), impact reduced (500s down from 6% -> 0.6%), nodes stabilizing.

incident-bot: Incident update saved to opslog: https://opslogs.prod/incidents/1740539876.

oncall-next: acknowledged. I'll post updates every 30m. :thumbsup:

maria: adding logs and alloc histograms to the incident folder. Postmortem owners: maria (eng-runtime), ra j (sre).

alex: thanks team. Will hand over to oncall-next and update support.

-- end of thread --
